Subject: Question re: final invoice split & VAT

Hi Sofia,

Quick one from procurement as we prepare the PO for renewal HLX-2028-RNWL-17. Our legal team has asked whether Redwood can split the final renewal invoice into two tranches to match internal milestone payments (70% on signature, 30% on go-live acceptance). The ask is driven by our fiscal year cut-off and the fact our EU entity will be the paying party for the second tranche.

Two specific questions:
- Can Redwood issue a split (two) invoices tied to the same contract and allow us to apply a reverse-charge VAT on the second tranche (our EU entity will self-account)?
- If not, what evidence do you need from our side (VAT reg. numbers, residency certificates) to avoid VAT being charged on the second tranche?

We want to avoid duplicate VAT charges and make sure the final settlement aligns with our PO timeline. I can attach the PO draft once we align on approach.

Appreciate a brief proposed flow so we can finalize PO today.

Thanks,
Amelia Turner
Head of Procurement 
Helix Health

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Question re: final invoice split & VAT

Hi Amelia,

Thanks — happy to outline a clean approach. Long story short: we can accommodate a two-tranche final invoice schedule and support reverse-charge on the EU-resident payment provided Helix supplies the necessary VAT registration and proof of place-of-supply. Proposed operational flow below:

1) Invoicing cadence
   - Invoice A (70%) — issued on signature date, standard invoice to the signing Helix entity. VAT treatment: charge VAT if the signing entity is non-EU or if we don't receive reverse-charge evidence.
   - Invoice B (30%) — issued on milestone (go-live acceptance). This invoice will be billed to the Helix EU entity and we can apply reverse-charge (VAT 0% on our side) if we receive:
     * Helix EU VAT number
     * Confirmation of EU entity name that will remit the payment
     * Statement of intent to self-account (short signed email is fine)

2) Evidence we need from Helix (send before Invoice B):
   - EU VAT number (registration certificate or VAT ID on invoice footer)
   - Billing entity legal name and billing address (for invoice B)
   - PO that references both tranches (helps our AP team)

3) Accounting ops & safeguards
   - Marcus (cc'd) will route Invoice B to the EU ledger once evidence is provided. We can hold Invoice B in a "pending evidence" state and time the issuance to match your acceptance date to prevent duplicate VAT accounting.
   - Proposal: Redwood issues Invoice A immediately after signature. We generate Invoice B as "pending" PDF; once Helix returns VAT number and PO, we finalize Invoice B and send for payment.

4) Escrow / tranche release (optional)
   - If Helix wants an escrow hold for the 30% tranche until software acceptance, we can route funds to an escrow account. Marcus: can finance provide an escrow wiring instruction if requested?

I've attached a draft invoice layout (HLX_Renewal_FinalInvoice_v3.pdf) with the split lines and placeholders for VAT/PO fields. Let me know if the PO team can confirm the EU paying entity and VAT number today — that will let us produce Invoice B with reverse-charge applied.

If you'd prefer a single invoice with payment instructions split internally on your side, we can do that too; downside is it requires Helix to self-manage VAT accounting between entities.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Enterprise Account Lead — Renewals
Redwood Inference
